entries.note: Honigberg 2010 PNAS (PMID 20615965, PMC2919935) resolves; probe sentence verbatim in abstract. untested is right: mouse-only, no human side. model_first_use_year 2010 fine.

Evans 2013 JPET (PMID 23709115) abstract carries the quote and itself pairs mouse-CIA occupancy-efficacy with human occupancy (comparison_stated true is right). Subjects are healthy volunteers, not patients; see rule question 3. Abstract-level only.
Same Honigberg 2010 abstract; occupancy-efficacy sentence verbatim. untested opener correct.

Full text read (PMC7496340). Methods sentence confirmed: doses chosen to reach plasma IC[subscript lost in PMC] 'as this extent of inhibition was correlated with efficacy in a rat collagen-induced arthritis model.' ANDES primary endpoint (ACR50 wk12, cohort 1) met at 150 mg QD p=0.016 and 200 mg BID p=0.0003, not at 50 mg QD p=0.25. Registry 2019-09-10 confirmed.

Fleischmann 2022 (PMID 38293957) quote verbatim, but it reports exposure AND target engagement reached - the dose prediction held. Inert-despite-engagement is an efficacy miss (already counted there). Drop this entry; dose cell ends at same 2020. source_calls_it should be null, not miss.

Honigberg 2010 abstract: CIA sentence verbatim. Model-side sources for later drugs also resolve: Crawford 2018 (PMID 29457982, rat), Goess 2019 (PMID 29862859, rat CIA, occupancy correlated), Park 2016 (PMID 27090981, mouse CIA).

Cohen 2020 abstract says 'demonstrates' (present tense) and uses MTX/RA abbreviations; otherwise identical. Paper names the rat arthritis model and reports patient ACR50, so the juxtaposition sits inside one source. Print 2020, epub 2020-04-09. same holds.

Genovese 2021 J Rheumatol 48(7):969 (PMID 33323529, epub 2020-12-15) abstract carries the quote; print year 2021 is correct under the brief. Registry 2019-10-09 confirmed. Under the brief's rule 5 (print year of the cited comparison) the order is same 2020 then contra 2021 - but see rule question 1 and missing.

Schafer 2020 (PMID 31721017, PMC7021855) full text: spermatid sentence verbatim. untested is right (no tox-vs-patient comparison found). Same source dates the male exclusion to trial start 2013-10-23, so rule 6 puts the opener and model_first_use_year at 2013, not 2020.

missing: Registry records are primary sources under rule 1 and would re-date the efficacy contra: NCT02638948 BMS-986142 (results posted 2019-05-28, ACR20/70 not met), NCT02628028 poseltinib (2019-10-09), NCT03233230 evobrutinib (2020-09-28, never published as a paper). All verified via ClinicalTrials.gov API v2. Citing the first gives contra 2019, ahead of ANDES (registry 2019-09-10, paper 2020).

Patient-level engagement: Schafer 2020 (10.1007/s40744-019-00182-7) median BTK occupancy 83-88% in RA patients at 375 mg/day. Not a status change if healthy-volunteer comparisons count; becomes the same entry (2020) if they do not.

Conaghan 2023 (PMID 38251590, Lancet Rheumatol 5:e263) confirmed: co-primary endpoints not met, 350 mg arm stopped at interim for elevated liver enzymes + no benefit; discussion names extent of BTK inhibition and drug distribution to inflamed sites as open questions. Supports efficacy contra; no safety comparison in it.
Nothing found for safety beyond the draft: patient signal is transaminase elevation (Cohen 2020 grade 3 ALT 3% at 200 mg BID; Conaghan 2023), no source says whether tox species predicted it.
rule_questions: Dating: rule 1 admits a registry record as a primary source but rule 2 demands a verbatim quote, which a registry record cannot supply, so drafters default to papers and print-year dating. Here the source-type choice flips the strip: papers give same 2020 then contra 2021; registry gives contra 2019-05 (BMS-986142) with the ANDES success also 2019-09, contra overrides, and the same never appears. Which does the house want? Under the brief as written the draft order stands.

Exposure-reached-but-inert (elsubrutinib, BMS-986142): which cell owns it? Recommend efficacy. The dose cell asks whether the model's exposure/occupancy target was reached in patients - it was ('adequate plasma exposure and target engagement'). Booking it in dose double-counts one fact as two contras and paints the PK/PD scaling as the failure when it was the one thing that translated. Caveat: Conaghan 2023 suggests blood occupancy may be the wrong target (synovial distribution), but no primary source shows that, so it stays a hypothesis.

Healthy-volunteer comparisons: the four questions say 'in patients'. Evans 2013 (engagement same, 2013) is healthy volunteers. If HV do not count, the engagement same moves to 2020 (Schafer 2020, RA patients). Dose same (Cohen 2020) is unaffected - patients.

Juxtaposed comparisons (comparison_stated false) for same/contra: checker brief item 3 reads as if they should be untested, but the house example ad-amyloid.json scores Doody 2013 as contra by juxtaposition. Accepted here on that precedent; the brief should say so explicitly.
